title: Proverbs 22
paragraphs: ¹ A good name is worth more than great riches, and to be held in loving esteem is better than silver or gold. ² The rich and the poor have this in common: the LORD is the maker of them all. ³ A prudent person sees danger coming and takes shelter, but the simple walk on and pay the price. ⁴ The reward of humility and the fear of the LORD is riches, honor, and life. ⁵ Thorns and snares lie in the path of the twisted; whoever guards their life will stay far from them.

⁶ Raise a child in the way they should go, and even when they are old they will not turn from it. ⁷ The rich rule over the poor, and the borrower is slave to the lender. ⁸ Whoever sows injustice will reap trouble, and the rod of their fury will fail. ⁹ A generous person will be blessed, for they share their food with the poor. ¹⁰ Drive out the mocker and conflict leaves with them; quarreling and insults come to an end.

¹¹ Whoever loves a pure heart and gracious speech will have the king for a friend. ¹² The eyes of the LORD watch over knowledge, but he overturns the plans of the faithless. ¹³ The lazy person says, "There is a lion outside! I will be killed in the street!" ¹⁴ The mouth of an immoral woman is a deep pit; whoever angers the LORD falls into it. ¹⁵ Foolishness is bound up in the heart of a child, but discipline will drive it far away.

¹⁶ Whoever oppresses the poor to enrich themselves, or gives to the wealthy, will only come to poverty. ¹⁷ Lean in and listen to the words of the wise; turn your heart to my teaching. ¹⁸ For it is good to keep these things in your heart and to have them always on your lips. ¹⁹ I am teaching you today — yes, you — so that your trust may be in the LORD. ²⁰ Have I not written to you thirty excellent sayings, offering counsel and knowledge, ²¹ to teach you true and reliable words, so you can give sound answers to those who send you?

²² Do not exploit the poor because they are poor, and do not crush the needy in court, ²³ for the LORD will take up their case and will plunder those who plunder them. ²⁴ Do not make friends with a hot-tempered person; do not associate with someone given to anger, ²⁵ or you may learn their ways and set a snare for yourself. ²⁶ Do not be one who shakes hands in a pledge or puts up security for debts; ²⁷ if you have nothing to pay, why should your bed be taken from under you?
²⁸ Do not move an ancient boundary stone set up by your ancestors. ²⁹ Do you see someone truly skilled at their work? They will serve before kings; they will not serve before obscure people.
